title: The Real Cost of an Electric Hypercar
description:
A Rimac Nevera went up for auction in the spring of twenty twenty-five, with only about thirteen hundred miles on the clock. Its window sticker said two million, three hundred eleven thousand dollars. The highest bid was one million, two hundred seventy thousand. And the car did not sell. This is what an electric hypercar really costs. Here is the twist. The electricity for all of those miles cost, by our own arithmetic, less than one hundred dollars. The part that cost a fortune was not the energy. It was owning a car that the market valued at roughly half of its sticker price.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
